name: oxplow-runtime
description: How oxplow tracks your work on its own (turns and requests), handoffs between threads, and the command bus. Loads on the oxplow `run_command` tool with oxplow.handoff.*, and on v_request, v_agent_turn or v_handoff.

# Your work in oxplow

oxplow tracks your work without your help. Nothing here is required: no
edit or stop waits on a task, and there's nothing to close before you
finish.

- **Recorded work.** The files you change (with edit tools or a shell)
  and the test runs you make are recorded against your turn, and through
  the turn against its request. A task you start (`oxplow.task.transition`
  to in progress) or file into progress becomes yours.
- **Turns.** Each turn records what opened it (`v_agent_turn.source`: a
  person, a background job's report, a subagent, another session) and how
  it ended; `v_turn_activity` says where its time went (tools, waiting on
  the person, the rest) and its compactions. A request (`v_request`) is a
  prompt and every turn it caused, with its live state; the tasks it
  worked on are `v_request_task`.
- **Session history.** In SQL the history of your conversations is
  `v_agent_session` (the slots opened on a thread), `v_agent_session_status`
  (each open session's last status), `v_agent_turn` (each prompt and
  answer), `v_tool_call` and `v_subagent`; the tasks a session's requests
  worked on are `v_request_task` joined to `v_task`. A session that lost its
  conversation is brought back with `oxplow.agent_session.reopen { session }`;
  the transcript page offers it.
- **Standing instructions.** What the person set for every session of
  your stream and of your thread is `v_stream.prompt` and `v_thread.prompt`
  (`SELECT s.prompt, t.prompt FROM v_thread t JOIN v_stream s ON s.id =
  t.stream_id`); they are already in your system prompt.
- **Waiting on the person.** When you need their answer, end your reply
  with the question: oxplow shows your thread as waiting on them. Nothing
  else is needed.
- **Handoffs.** Work another thread hands you arrives at the start of a
  prompt in a `<handoffs>` block. Take it on or decline it with
  `oxplow.handoff.resolve`; to hand work to another thread, see
  `references/commands.md`. Nothing wakes the other agent.
- **Context basket.** A `<context-basket>` block is what the person
  collected for you; read each `[oxplow uri …]` with `oxplow_read`.
- **Hints.** oxplow may add short, advisory guidance to your next prompt
  or tool result (work grown large with nothing committed, metric movement).

## Writing about work

Refer to a task by its quoted title, never by id or "#N": the person
can't map ids to what they see. Write entities in task bodies, summaries
and wiki pages as `[[…]]` wikilinks (syntax: the oxplow-wiki-capture skill).
Inline code is for identifiers and snippets.

# Commands (the one write path)

State changes are **commands**. `list_commands` lists what you may run (ids
and summaries); `list_commands { id }` (or `{ prefix: "oxplow.handoff." }`)
shows a command's input schema and an example input: read it before a
command's first run and copy the example's shape. `run_command { id, input }`
runs one. Every run is validated, policy-checked and audited; undoable runs
return an `inverse`.

Invalid input names the failing field, what it accepts and the example
input; a denial says why. A run that needs the person's confirmation
returns `{ kind: "proposed", proposal, message }` and waits in their
Alerts. Tell them what you proposed and why; don't run it again or look
for another way to make the change.

`references/commands.md`: project config keys (`oxplow.config.*`, and which
need confirmation), the families of commands, offloading a read-heavy
question to an Explore subagent through a note, and handing work to
another thread.

description: Answering questions about the project's history and code from oxplow's own data — who changed what and when, which branches exist and how far apart, where a symbol is defined, what a file declares, which files have errors, and the errors the person saw in the app. Loads on v_op_error, v_commit, v_commit_file, v_branch, v_branch_divergence, v_commit_between, v_tag, v_symbol, v_diagnostic, oxplow_code_definition, oxplow_code_references, oxplow_code_symbols, and when the user asks "who changed X", "when did X change", "history of X", "what branches", "where is X defined", "what's in this file", "what calls X", "what's broken", or "can you see that error" / "the red error toast".

# The project's history and code

oxplow keeps the repository's history and the code as SQL datasets.
Read them with `oxplow_query_sql` before `git log` or grep. `v_field`
documents each column.

## History (`v_commit`, `v_commit_file`, `v_branch`, `v_tag`)

- **`v_commit`** — one row per commit (`sha`, `author`, `email`,
  `committed_at`, `subject`, `body`, `parents`), refreshed on boot and
  whenever refs move, for every stream's branch.
- **`v_commit_file`** — the files each commit changed (`sha`, `path`,
  `status`, `additions`, `deletions`). Join it to `v_commit` on `sha`:

  ```sql
  SELECT c.sha, c.subject, c.committed_at FROM v_commit c
  JOIN v_commit_file f ON f.sha = c.sha
  WHERE f.path = 'src/lib.rs' ORDER BY c.committed_at DESC LIMIT 20
  ```

  Who last changed each line: the `oxplow_vcs_blame { path, revision? }` tool (`working`,
  `snap:<id>` or `git:<rev>`; an uncommitted line names no commit).
  Quick answers have a tool each (`references/history.md`); history past
  the index (any revision, one path, paged) is `oxplow_vcs_log`.
- **`v_branch`** — branches (`name`, `kind`, `head_sha`, `is_default`,
  the `stream_id` that has it checked out, and for a local one its
  `upstream`, `ahead`, `behind`); **`v_tag`** — tags. A `v_stream` row's
  `head_sha` is where its workspace is. Uncommitted files: `v_change_file`
  of the `v_change` with `kind = 'working'` (`staged`, `untracked`).
- **`v_file`** — a folder's entries (`references/code.md`).
- **`v_branch_divergence`**, **`v_commit_between`** — two revisions
  compared, the commits between (`references/history.md`).

Changing history (commit, merge, rebase, push, checkout): the
`oxplow.vcs.*` commands (`list_commands`) or `git` in your terminal. One
commit's worth of change, from the commit page: `oxplow.git.cherry_pick {
stream, rev }` applies a commit the branch doesn't carry, `oxplow.git.revert
{ stream, rev }` undoes one it does.

## Code (`v_symbol`, `v_diagnostic`, `v_lsp_server`, the `code_*` tools)

`references/code.md` (oxplow_get_skill reference `code`) has columns, symbol
kinds, examples and the live-server tools. In short: `v_symbol` is
where something is defined and what a file declares (from oxplow's own
parsing, no language server needed); `v_diagnostic` is what the language
servers report now (`SELECT path, count(*) FROM v_diagnostic WHERE
severity = 'error' GROUP BY path`); `v_lsp_server` says which servers exist
and run; "what calls X" and anything the stored view can't know go to the
`code_*` MCP tools.

## Errors the person saw (`v_op_error`)

When an operation fails in front of the person (a merge, a push, a save)
they get a red toast and a row on the Alerts page. Each is recorded, so
"can you see that error?" is answerable:

- **`v_op_error`** — one row per failure (`at`, `label` — what they were
  doing — `command`, `message`, `exit_code`, `signal`, `duration_ms`,
  `thread`, `stream_id`, `output_size` (the output's length), `seen` and
  `dismissed` (the person opened / cleared it)). The latest:
  `SELECT event_id, at, label, command, message FROM v_op_error ORDER BY
  at DESC LIMIT 5`.
- **The output itself** is `v_op_error_output` (`event_id`, `stderr`,
  `stdout`). A row with `output_size` NULL captured nothing; its
  `message` is all.
- How long they keep, and whose: `references/history.md`.
